subject: Follow-up: ShopLytics embeddings architecture & next actions
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@shoplytics.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: ShopLytics embeddings architecture & next actions

Hi Samir / Nina —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to summarize the key points from our discovery so we all have the same expectations and next steps. I’ve attached a short cost/POC proposal and the usage worksheet you asked for.

High-level recap (what you told us)
- Primary goal: improve product-search relevance by reranking the top 50 results using dense embeddings + contextual rerank.
- Current stack: Milvus for vector store, Redis-based LRU cache in front of the index, metadata in Postgres, custom FAISS worker for offline reindexing.
- Index scale: ~120M active product vectors (embedding dim 768), growing ~1.5M items/month.
- Traffic/throughput: average 40 qps; anticipated peak bursts ~200 qps during promos; batch re-ranks from nightly jobs produce spikes up to 600 qps-equivalent for short windows.
- Cost target: long-term goal <$0.002 per query (rerank unit).
- Latency/SLOs: 99th percentile end-to-end (embedding + lookup + rerank) target < 120 ms for interactive search; acceptable background batch latency is higher.
- Pain points: cold-cache tail latency (slow disk-backed shards), managing reindex window that causes CPU/GPU contention, and unclear cost per 100k queries across current infra.

Success criteria for POC
1) Demonstrate 99p < 120ms on a representative subset (10M vectors) for 95qps synthetic workload with realistic cache miss rates.
2) Unit cost estimate for production traffic (baseline + expected growth) with clear knobs (batching, quantization, cache TTL) to meet the <$0.002 target.
3) Ops playbook: safe nightly reindex pattern and autoscaling plan to avoid promo spikes causing outages.

Next steps (proposed)
- Action 1 (this week): Camila to run architecture fit / kernel recommendation after we get a sample export (schema + 10k vectors + typical query set).
- Action 2 (by 5/25): Redwood to deliver a short POC plan + cost model and proposed caching strategy (attached draft).
- Action 3 (week of 6/1): 60–90 minute technical deep dive + environment access to run a small-scale benchmark (we recommend 10M vectors on a dedicated POC cluster).

Attachments: shoplytics-usage-estimates-202605.xlsx, redwood-embeddings-proposal-v1.pdf (contains proposed POC config and cost estimates).

Questions / clarifications I recorded from the call
- Confirm index growth: you said ~1.5M/month active items — is that net new or after TTL/retirements?
- Can you share a typical top-50 query log sample and distribution of vector lengths / tokenization details for the product text?

If that matches your notes, I’ll kick off the POC docs and Camila will reach out to arrange the sample export details. Thanks — Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes

From: Samir Rao <samir@shoplytics.com>

Cc: Nina Patel <nina@shoplytics.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ShopLytics embeddings architecture & next actions

Thanks Rafael — this is a good summary and aligns with our notes. A couple of clarifications: 

- Index size: we currently estimate ~120M active vectors (not counting deprecated SKUs); growth of ~1.5M net per month is correct.
- Stack: Milvus managed by our infra team + Redis cache in front. We also have an internal bloom-filter microservice to reduce cold-shard lookups.
- Batch patterns: nightly re-rank job re-embeds ~50k changed items and a weekly partial full-reindex for regions; those windows are what create the short spikes — so anything that helps smooth or stagger reindexes would be ideal.
- Budget: $/query target is aggressive; we want a clear tradeoff matrix (latency vs cost vs accuracy) before committing.

I attached our internal SLO extract (search-slos.pdf) to the thread offline — I’ll drop it to your drive folder.

For next steps, please:
1) include a simple cache strategy that addresses cold-cache tail at 99p (e.g., pre-warming / hot-shard replication or serving cold tail from a cheaper replica with graceful degradation),
2) give an initial cost projection for both hosted vs dedicated deployment choices, and
3) confirm what telemetry you’ll need (e.g., top-queries, distribution of vector update sizes, cache hit-rate history).

Happy to meet for the deep dive. Wed 6/2 or Thu 6/3 after 10am PT works for Nina and me.

Thanks — Samir

Thanks for the detail, Samir / Rafael — quick technical notes from my side: 

- For 120M vectors at dim=768 we typically recommend quantization (8-bit or product quantization) + KV cache for hot keys. That usually gets 2–3x cost reduction with modest accuracy impact; we'll include accuracy delta tests in the POC.
- To address the nightly spike I suggest two options we’ll model: (A) staggered incremental reindex (micro-batches spread over the low-traffic window) + write-ahead change log, or (B) offload reindexing to a separate GPU pool with async sync to the main read path. Both are implementable during POC.
- Telemetry we'll need: top-50 query set (CSV), 30-day histogram of query qps, cache hit-rate by shard (if available), and a sample export of 10k vectors + metadata.

I can provision a temporary POC config and run the 10M vector benchmark once we have the sample and a confirmed test window. Rafael — can you share the sample export instructions (S3 or signed URL)?

Thanks — Camila

--
